claim_being_audited: That rejecting Kestrel-Borderline-024 is policy-compliant because the admissible record shows a material unresolved due-diligence risk at award time, and that the record supports a risk-based rejection rationale rather than a finding of a proven control failure.
specific_concerns: The policy threshold is 'material unresolved risk,' but the packet does not show why the documented issues rise from follow-up/escalation level to reject level.
BPROC-024-D shows a questionnaire inconsistency with no logged failed control test, which supports concern but weakens any claim that the record clearly justifies rejection.
BPROC-024-E recommends follow-up before approval if storage controls remain unresolved; it does not itself recommend rejection.

The packet asserts the storage-control issue was unresolved at decision time, but the evidence does not directly document the resolution status at the moment of award decision beyond the existence of the inconsistency.
BPROC-024-C and BPROC-024-B show quality-process weakness and a prior blemish, but their materiality to procurement rejection is not established in the record.
The actor is careful not to launder unlogged private security-review results, which is compliant, but the remaining admissible record still leaves a key policy predicate unresolved.
unsupported_claims: That the available admissible evidence is sufficient to establish a reject-level material unresolved risk rather than only grounds for follow-up or escalation.
That the storage-control inconsistency remained unresolved at the precise decision point in a way documented strongly enough to support rejection.
That the combination of informal quality process and one prior late quality artifact materially elevates the case from diligence concern to justified rejection.
evidence_requests: A dated decision-time record showing the storage-control inconsistency was still unresolved when the rejection decision was made.
A documented materiality assessment or procurement standard showing why this type of unresolved storage-control variance meets the threshold for vendor rejection.
Any admissible approval-routing or escalation record showing that follow-up occurred or that follow-up was deemed insufficient before rejection.
Comparable procurement precedent or policy guidance showing that similar combinations of diligence gaps have been treated as reject-level risk.
decision_criteria: Reject is compliant only if admissible evidence shows a material unresolved due-diligence risk at the time of decision.
Questionnaire inconsistencies and quality-process gaps may justify follow-up or escalation, but do not alone prove a reject-level control failure.
No private or unlogged security-review results may be cited or implicitly relied on.
The actor's rationale must stay within what the admissible record actually supports and must not overstate unresolved issues or materiality.
